Countdown to Christmas with Neuhaus’ stunning chocolate story book advent calendar. The smart red book opens up to reveal 25 doors - once all the doors have been opened a festive scene is revealed. One of Belgium’s finest chocolatiers, these filled pralines are some of the very best we’ve tasted. The glossy, silky smooth chocolate is delicately flavoured and truly melts in the mouth.

Behind each of the 25 doors is a Neuhaus chocolate, from dark hazelnut gianduja to coffee nougat, spiced biscuit praline to soft caramel. The selection of white, milk and dark Belgian chocolates in fruit and nut flavours means this Advent calendar has something for every chocolate connoisseur.

Looking for more? Check out our full range of food advent calendars or see our pick of food advent calendars for 2026.

About Neuhaus

Neuhaus Chocolates are one of the finest chocolate houses in Belgium – and perhaps the world. The silky smooth chocolate is beautifully delicate and has a wonderful snap, all blended with exquisite ingredients, carefully sourced for the very best flavour. The iconic chocolatiers are also heralded as the inventors of Belgian filled pralines. Neuhaus uses 100% sustainably sourced cacao for their chocolates as well as investing in their own cacao plantation in Ecuador. Any ingredients that are added to the chocolates, be it nuts, fruit or coffee, are 100% natural.

Neuhaus was started by Jean Neuhaus in 1857. He opened a pharmacy in Brussels, and as a way to thrill his customers, he covered their medicines in a thin layer of chocolate. Fast forward to 1912, Jean’s grandson swapped medicine for an indulgent chocolate centre, inventing what we now know and love as the praline.

About Netherton Foundry

The Netherton Foundry is a family company based in Shropshire – home of the 18th and 19th century ironmasters. Their pans are made from 99.1% pure iron and they use locally sourced materials wherever possible – the oak that makes the pan handles is British, and the flax seasoning oil comes from Sussex. Experienced local craftsmen use traditional manufacturing methods to bring you high quality cookware that gets better over time.

products.title: Ferndale Vista Cookware
products.body_html:
Netherton Foundry’s spun iron frying pan is the non-stick pan for those who hate non-stick pans. Unlike better-known Teflon which can peel or scratch after a year, the surface of a spun iron pan becomes more non-stick over time. Year after year, you’ll build a patina of cooking memories that you can pass down the generations – along with the pan! Use this 8-inch frying pan to make an omelette for one, frittata for two or make thin and crispy pancakes by swirling batter around the base of the pan.

Please note this product has no packaging.

Made from Netherton Foundry’s signature spun iron, the frying pan is lighter than cast iron but still has the sought after non-stick, patina-building qualities and durability. Suitable for all cooking surfaces including induction hobs, the frying pan heats fast and cools quickly. It also comes pre-seasoned, so you can get cooking right away. You can even remove the oak handle covers so you can use the pan in the oven or under the grill. Before the first use, wash the pan with hot water. Do not use soap or detergent. Dry immediately with a towel, as leaving to air dry increases the chance of rusting. If you need to scrub, use a plastic bristled brush in hot soapy water, but avoid anything harsher. Avoid detergents completely.

The Netherton Foundry is a family company based in Shropshire – home of the 18th and 19th century ironmasters. Caution: if using a ceramic or induction hob, increase the heat slowly for the first few uses to prevent buckling. Do not drop hot pans into cold water – this can cause the metal to warp or shatter. Not dishwasher safe.

French classics are taken to a new level, as well as twists on global recipes.

  • ‘Viking Smoked Salt’ has a deliclously smoky flavour and is perfect for topping your scrambled eggs or rubbed on steak before searing.
  • Nepalese ‘timur berry’ brings extraordinary grapefruit notes to a mini tartelletes au citron.
  • Try speculoos spice blend for festive biscuits,
  • A persillade spice blend with bear's garlic(wild garlic) will be your ideal pairing for any Mediterranean dishes, and works especially well with mussels.

This is a flavour packed way to countdown to Christmas from the finest spice merchants in the world.

Looking for more? Check out our full range of food advent calendars or see our pick of food advent calendars for 2026.

⭐ About Terre Exotique - an extraordinary spice merchant

Terre Exotique works directly with specialist farmers and producers around the world – to find the very best peppers, spices and salts on the planet.

The company was founded by Erwann de Kerros, a Breton and seasoned traveller. After time spent managing the Penja pepper plantation in Cameroon, Kerros started hunting down other specialist peppers and spices – and Terre Exotique was born.

The company works closely with farmers to preserve natural habitats, and to ensure a sustainable income for local communities. Discover hundreds of flavours from around the world, with the unrivalled Terre Exotique selection.

🌱 Let Erwann take you to source timur berry in Nepal...🌱

“First stop is deep in the local markets, the favourite hunting ground for any spice hunter. A synesthetic experience, and an invitation to travel. In shops and stalls, I smell the soul of the country, I take its pulse, I sense its custom and its commerce... I imagine the essence of its cuisine.

"I find a refined and utterly subtle powdered ginger, a rare and precious black cardamom dried over fire, delicate timur berries that grow wild in the Mahabharat hills between the Terai and the Pahar regions… This is Christmas in July! But spontaneous enthusiasm aside, we must now separate the good seeds that we want for Terre Exotique from the chaff that is here for the tourists. We must know which are imported products and which are native spices.”

Discover the timur berry Erwann selects only for Terre Exotique inside this Advent calendar.

About Neuhaus

Neuhaus Chocolates are one of the finest chocolate houses in Belgium – and perhaps the world. The silky smooth chocolate is beautifully delicate and has a wonderful snap, all blended with exquisite ingredients, carefully sourced for the very best flavour. The iconic chocolatiers are also heralded as the inventors of Belgian filled pralines. Neuhaus uses 100% sustainably sourced cacao for their chocolates as well as investing in their own cacao plantation in Ecuador. Any ingredients that are added to the chocolates, be it nuts, fruit or coffee, are 100% natural.

Neuhaus was started by Jean Neuhaus in 1857. He opened a pharmacy in Brussels, and as a way to thrill his customers, he covered their medicines in a thin layer of chocolate. Fast forward to 1912, Jean’s grandson swapped medicine for an indulgent chocolate centre, inventing what we now know and love as the praline.

The Ankarsrum Assistent Original Stand Mixer in Harmony Beige is the Swedish stand mixer for people who truly love to bake.

The first thing to know is that Ankarsrum mixes unlike other stand mixers. The 7L stainless steel bowl rotates, while the arm, roller and scraper stay in place. It feels unusual at first if you are used to a tilt-head mixer. Then you watch a dough come together without climbing a hook, and it starts to make sense!

  • 7L stainless steel bowl for large batches
  • Powerful 1500W motor in the base
  • Rotating bowl with fixed mixing arm
  • Includes dough, whisking and beating tools
  • Stylish neutral colour

The roller and scraper let you adjust how the dough moves, which is especially useful with wet sourdoughs and heavier wholegrain mixes. There is also a dough hook for firmer doughs, plus a 3.5L beater bowl with whisks and beaters for cream, eggs, cakes and biscuits.

The built-in timer is extremely useful. The machine stops when the time is up. It is also known for being steadier and less noisy than many high-power mixers, which matters more than you think when dough needs a long knead.

Use a fillet or two to start a tomato sauce, melt into olive oil with garlic for spaghetti, or lay over hot buttered toast with a squeeze of lemon. They are strong, so you do not need many. That is part of their charm.

Meet the maker: Rizzoli

The Rizzoli family are master anchovy curers. The company has been passed down through five generations of the same family.

Perhaps surprisingly, they are based in Parma, the land-locked city more famous for its ham. However, Parma is also on the ancient salt road from the port of Genoa, and (in 1892) was the epicentre of Italy's tomato canning revolution. Founding brothers Luigi and Emilio Rizzoli spotted potential to combine the booming canning industry with the city's trade routes and launched what has become one of Italy's best-known anchovy brands.

The signature product was born in that first year: anchovies in spicy sauce. Rizzoli Emanuelli still describes the sauce as a secret family recipe.

Product formulations and details may change. For the latest ingredients and allergen information always check product packaging prior to consumption. Ingredients: anchovies (42%), extra virgin olive oil (39%), vinegar (9%), tuna, wine, sugar, mustard, spices, carrots, onions, salt.

Semipreserved. Keep in a dry and cool place. Once open, keep in the fridge covered with sauce.

products.title: Ferndale Wren Cookbook
products.body_html:
A mother’s recipes and her daughter’s first kitchen adventures away from home. Dear Grace is a warm and wise cookbook written by chef and award-winning food writer Claire Thomson for her daughter as she leaves home for university – one for parents to read, and their soon to be adult children to cook from. Claire began addressing Instagram posts to Grace, each pairing heartfelt advice and reminiscences with a recipe to cook and why it would fit the bill, hundreds of miles away from home.

This struck a chord with parents everywhere experiencing similar emotional highs and lows as they sent their children off into adult life. Including the chapters: Legacy Recipes, Cooking on a Budget, All Back to Mine – Late Night Food, Flatshare Feasts, Faster than Fast Food and Sweet Tooth – these are simple, accessible recipes for cooking nutritious food on a budget. Through memories and stories of family and food, Claire perfectly captures the bittersweet moment of watching your child begin their independent life – and the comfort of knowing they can feed themselves and their friends with confidence and creativity.

products.body_html:
Discover the rich, complex flavour of artisanal Balsamic Vinegar of Modena. The Sous Chef Balsamic Vinegar of Modena IGP is made by a family producer, now in its 17th generation of harvesting, pressing and aging grapes in Modena.

Sun-ripened grapes are pressed and aged for at least 12 years - creating a rich, thick balsamic vinegar. It has deep sweet-sour notes of prune, raisin and smoky oak.

  • Made in Modena, the heartland of balsamic vinegar
  • Sun-ripened grapes for natural sweetness
  • Aged in wooden barrels for at least 12 years
  • Sweet-sharp notes of prune and raisins
  • Protected IGP ingredient status

Grapes are sun-ripened on the vine long enough to develop a rich raisin sweetness. They are harvested and pressed, then simmered very gently for a full 24 hours. 

The resulting glossy thick and caramelised juice is the precious grape must. Grape must is then aged in wooden barrels, which bring their own oaky rich flavour.

As the balsamic vinegar ages over many years, it slowly evaporates - concentrating the flavour and bringing lovely complex notes of smoky sweetness.

In fact, the barrels used to make this incredible Italian condiment are never emptied. The master 'vinegar taster' artfully blends different barrels, constantly adjusting levels and sampling the contents to create the most delicious blend possible.

So while the balsamic in your bottle is at least 12 years old, it's possibly blended with some barrels that are even older. This is a fabulous balsamic that brings instant depth and interest to both sweet and savoury dishes.

Product formulations and details may change. For the latest ingredients and allergen information always check product packaging prior to consumption. Ingredients: cooked grape must, wine vinegar (sulphites).

Dudu Eats Lemongrass chilli oil is handmade in small batches. Inspired by the flavours of Thailand, it adds instant heat to stir fries and noodle soups.

This fiery condiment is a labour of love. It has a slow-cooked, naturally fermented base of shallots, garlic and galangal. The bright, citrusy flavour of lemongrass shines through. Soy sauce and shiitake mushrooms create layers of umami, while peanuts add subtle crunch.

Drizzle Dudu Eats chilli oil over fried rice and noodle salads. It’s fantastic in dipping sauces for wontons and chicken satay. The aroma of Thai herbs transforms the simplest of dishes. We love its nutty crunch and satisfying spicy kick.

Dudu Eats chilli oil is handmade by a mother-and-daughter duo. It’s the brainchild of Romany Henry, a culinary-trained chef and food content creator. She was born in Hong Kong and raised in Phuket. Now living in London, Romany shares her passion for food and travel on social media.

Store in a cool and dry place, away from direct sunlight. Refrigerate after opening.

Product formulations and details may change. For the latest ingredients and allergen information always check product packaging prior to consumption. Ingredients: Groundnut oil (peanuts), dried chilli flakes, shiitake mushrooms, umami paste (sake, mirin, soy), shallots, garlic, reduced salt & gluten-free soy sauce, sugar, capers, salt, lemongrass (4%), lime leaf, galangal, peanuts, monosodium glutamate, kombu stock powder (kelp)..

Allergy advice: For allergens see ingredients listed in bold. May contain traces of nuts, sesame, mustard and lupins.

Meet the maker: Apicoltura Cazzola

Apicoltura Cazzola is a nomadic beekeeping producer in the Bologna area of Emilia-Romagna. The beekeepers move their 300+ hives with the seasons and the flowering. It is a very direct way of following the landscape. When the flowers change, the honey changes too. Meanwhile, the honey is left as natural as possible - it isn't heat treated for example. Apicoltura's mantra is simple, and rather lovely: “Why change what nature has already made perfectly.”

Product formulations and details may change. For the latest ingredients and allergen information always check product packaging prior to consumption. Ingredients: apricots, grape sugar, lemon juice.

Storage: store in a dark, dry place. Once opened, keep refrigerated at 2-4 degrees C and consume shortly thereafter.

The DOAP Charcoal Classic Silicone Dough Cleaning Bar is one of the most exciting innovations for bakers that we've seen in years! This one is a dark grey colour - choose between the different DOAP colours here.

It looks like a small bar of soap, but it is made from soft food-grade platinum silicone, with flexible little nubs that help lift sticky dough from hands, bowls, starter jars and dough tubs using water.

It feels gentle on hands, while thoroughly removing dough from all the nooks and crannies: around knuckles, under nails, along the inside curve of a mixing bowl. Keep one by the sink, and never put a dough-ruined sponge in the bin again!

  • Soft silicone nubs remove sticky dough
  • Made in small batches in Nashville
  • Food-grade platinum silicone, hand-safe tested
  • Useful for hands, bowls and jars
  • Dishwasher safe and easy to rinse

It is made from ultra-high purity, food-grade platinum silicone, with a flexible feel that is firm. After use, leave the bar in water for 10–15 minutes so any dough softens, then rinse, wash with a little dish soap, and let it dry on the rack.

"One of the more useful, practical inventions and innovations in the kitchen we've seen in a long time." Sorted Food

Meet the maker: DOAP

DOAP is the result of one baker's frustration - facing a problem that many fellow bakers will recognise. Joshua Grange invented his revolutionary silicone 'soap' after growing tired of sticky dough clinging to his hands after every bake, and ruining traditional sponges.

Determined to find a solution, he designed a simple silicone scrubber that removes dough using nothing but water.

Every DOAP is handmade in Nashville from premium American-made silicone. Exclusively available in the UK, at Sous Chef.

Vietnamese dishes are often thought of as time-consuming and intricate, likely due to the popularity of the country’s famously delicious but complex dish, Pho. However, there are many dishes that, with the right ingredients and a little know-how, come together in no time and, even better, in just one pan! Discover just how easy it is to create Vietnamese flavours without the fuss in Thuy Diem Pham's latest book, One Pan Vietnam. Packed with simple and mouth-watering Vietnamese-style recipes for everything from stir-fries and salads to broths and bún bowls, you’ll find aromatic noodle soups, delicious salads bursting with fresh, zesty flavours, heart-warming soups and stews, and much more.

Using Thuy’s tips and techniques, you can make fresh and wonderfully flavoursome Vietnamese-style, restaurant-quality meals at home, with remarkably minimal mess.

products.title: Daily Basket Solace Cookbook
products.body_html:
Consider the Anchovy, food journalist and anchovy lover Sudi Pigott goes on a journey of discovery to find out more about the little fish with the big flavour. Travelling from Cantabria to California, in this book you will meet the personalities, families and communities whose livelihood depends on the not-so humble anchovy, participating in traditions celebrating the little fish, visiting bars, festivals and even museums devoted exclusively to anchovies.

See the flatbottomed barque boats and tightly packed fishermen's cottages of Collioure that inspired Matisse, Derain and Fauvism. Meet the film star who made a short film on the sex life of the anchovy. Dig into the preserving traditions of Ancient Greece.

'Not just an elegant love letter to the anchovy, but the only book you'll ever need on one of the world's greatest ingredients' Tom Parker Bowles

'A gloriously geeky, deeply researched and hugely entertaining journey that gives this small fish the epic treatment it deserves' Heston Blumenthal

'Between these covers is an anchovy odyssey, a journey in search of a small fish of enormous importance. Fascinating, unexpected and utterly enticing!' Rachel Roddy

Uncork the garum of Ancient Rome and compare it to its modern counterpart, Colatura d'Alici, aged in bourbon barrels. Alongside delicious recipes to close each chapter, this book is rich in research, stuffed with maverick, rakish characters and full of flavour. Whether you love them or you hate them, Consider the Anchovy is both an entertaining odyssey and an unabashedly passionate manifesto that celebrates anchovies with their pungent, complex, umami allure as leading, albeit sometimes unpredictable, movers in world culinary history.

'A beautiful subject and fascinating read from a passionate anchovy missionary' Claudia Roden

'Fascinating in every way - a Cod for the 21st century' Giles Coren

'As vital as sunshine to brighten even the dullest day, the anchovy, with its unique presence, holds great sway in the kitchen and at the table, now in this ace book' Jeremy Lee

'Sudi Pigott is perhaps one of the best food writers that I have known in my long career. I love her new book, which is written with passion, very informative and well-researched. The book brought my culinary horizons to new heights and will bring yours as well!' Ken Hom CBE

A delicious collection of fuss-free pasta recipes from your favourite chefs and recipe creators Pasta is comfort - easy, familiar, endlessly satisfying. But too often we get stuck in the loop of the same recipes: a trusty bolognese, a jar of pesto, the reliable carbonara. What if pasta could be more?This book is an invitation to rethink pasta: to explore fresh flavours, global influences, and unexpected pairings that bring new joy to the table.

From their home in Cumbria, Northern Pasta Co. has pioneered spelt pasta made from British grains, and in their first cookbook they share recipes of their own alongside favourites from celebrated chefs and food creators, including: Max La Manna's Zesty Radiatori Summer Salad Olia Hercules's Rigatoni from Napoli via Genoa & Odesa Izzie Cox's Miso Gochujang Pumpkin Rigatoni Helen Graham's Tomato & Tamarind Gigli Tom Jackson's Slow-cooked Courgette Casarecce Saliha Khan's Desi Meema Rigatoni From sauce-hugging shapes to bold, flavour-packed combinations, these recipes prove pasta is never boring. It's time to fall in love with it all over again.

It's the fabulous quality extra virgin olive oil that makes this spread excellent. The flavour is truly pistachio, sweetened slightly, followed by the rich, savoury, nutty olive oil notes.

Joe & Seph’s Goats Cheese & Cracked Black Pepper Popcorn is a savoury popcorn for people who usually reach for the cheese board before the sweet tin. The goats cheese gives it a tangy, creamy bite, while Malabar black pepper brings warmth and a little fragrant heat. It feels made for opening with drinks, especially when friends are standing around the kitchen and dinner is still half an hour away.

  • Made with 23% dried goats cheese
  • Warm kick from Malabar black pepper
  • Handcrafted gourmet popcorn from London
  • Savoury, tangy, grown-up snacking

Meet the maker: Joe & Seph's

Product formulations and details may change. For the latest ingredients and allergen information always check product packaging prior to consumption. Ingredients: Corn, sunflower oil, dried goats cheese (milk) (23%), malabar black pepper, salt.

Allergy advice: For allergens see ingredients in bold. May contain: made in an environment where gluten, eggs, nuts, sesame, peanuts, soy, sulphites, celery and mustard are present.

Store in a cool, dry, dark place. Once opened consume within 5 days.

products.title: Ferndale Orbis Ingredient
products.body_html:
Joe & Seph’s Marmite Popcorn is one for the Marmite people. Air-popped corn is coated in smooth caramel, then finished with Marmite yeast extract for that sweet, salty, savoury hit that makes you reach back into the bag before you’ve quite decided what you think.

  • Crunchy caramel with Marmite® savoury depth
  • Air-popped corn, not fried
  • Handmade by Joe & Seph’s in Britain
  • No artificial flavours or colours
  • Suitable for vegetarians

Meet the maker: Joe & Seph's

Joe & Seph’s is a London family business making gourmet popcorn and caramel sauces by hand.

They launched in 2010 with one clear goal: to make the best-tasting popcorn in the world. Since then, their small team of pastry chefs has created more than 50 popcorn flavours, from classic sweet and savoury recipes to playful, dessert-inspired ideas.

The popcorn is air-popped, rather than cooked in oil. This gives it a light, crisp texture, ready for coating in caramel, chocolate, spices or savoury seasonings. Each batch is handmade in London using 100% natural ingredients.

Product formulations and details may change. For the latest ingredients and allergen information always check product packaging prior to consumption. Ingredients: Corn, butter (milk), sugar, marmite® yeast extract (18%) {yeast extract (barley) (wheat), (oat), (rye) salt, vegetable juice concentrate, vitamins (thiamin, ribolflavin, niacin, vitamin b12, folic acid), natural flavouring (celery)}, corn syrup, marmite® yeast extract flavour {yeast extract, lactose (milk), salt, sugar, citric acid, onion powder, rapeseed oil, garlic powder, natural flavouring (celery), marmite® (yeast extract (barley), salt, vegetable extracts, vitamins)}.

Allergy advice: For allergens see ingredients in bold. May contain: made in an environment where eggs, nuts, peanuts, soy, sulphites and mustard are present.

Store in a cool, dry, dark place. Once opened consume within 5 days.

  • Air-popped popcorn with smooth caramel coating
  • Flavoured with real gin and tonic
  • Citrus, juniper, tonic, then gin
  • Handmade in London in small batches
  • A fun gift for gin lovers

The corn is air-popped, then coated in caramel and peanut butter, so you get that brittle caramel crunch first, followed by a smooth peanut richness.

  • Caramel-coated popcorn with peanut butter richness
  • Air-popped corn, crisp and crunchy
  • Handmade in London in small batches
  • Contains 25% peanuts and butter
  • Good for films, gifting and sharing

The corn is coated with pure maple syrup, then mixed with chunky roasted pecan pieces, so you get that sticky-sweet maple flavour first, followed by buttery crunch and toasted nut.

  • Pure maple syrup in every handful
  • Chunky roasted pecans for real crunch
  • Handmade in Great Britain
  • Good for films, guests or gifting

products.title: Ferndale Pike Ingredient
products.body_html:
Joe & Seph’s Toffee Apple & Cinnamon Popcorn is a sweet, buttery caramel popcorn with little pieces of apple folded through the coating. It has that fairground toffee apple feeling, but in a bag you can open on the sofa. The cinnamon comes in after the caramel, giving it a warm, baked-apple note rather than a sharp spice hit.

  • Sweet toffee with real apple pieces
  • Warm cinnamon in the finish
  • Air-popped popcorn, coated in caramel
  • Handmade in Great Britain
  • Contains milk from real butter

This is the sort of popcorn I’d put out in a bowl before a film, then wonder why half of it has gone before the trailers finish. The apple pieces give the odd chewy bite, which makes it feel more like a little pudding than a plain snack.

Try it with hot chocolate, mulled apple juice, or a scoop of vanilla ice cream

products.title: Greenbank Nova Ingredient
products.body_html:
Joe & Seph’s Orange Chocolate Popcorn is a sweet, chocolate-coated gourmet popcorn coated with Belgian milk and dark chocolate, then finished with orange peel and orange oil for a zesty chocolate-orange flavour.

It feels more like a small confectionery treat than a regular bag of popcorn. Good for movie nights, passing round after supper, or adding to a gift hamper when you want something a bit more fun than another box of chocolates.

  • Belgian milk and dark chocolate coating
  • Zesty orange peel and orange oil
  • Handmade by Joe & Seph’s in Britain
  • Sweet, crisp, chocolate-orange popcorn
  • Lovely for gifting or sharing

Serve in a bowl after dinner with coffee, or put the pouch out with nuts, biscuits and clementines for an easy festive nibble.

The corn is air-popped, then coated in buttery caramel made with real Guinness beer, so you get sweetness first, then those malty, roasted notes, and a small hit of coffee at the end.

  • Made with 22% real Guinness beer
  • Buttery caramel with malty stout notes
  • Subtle coffee finish for gentle bitterness
  • Handmade in small batches in London
  • Air-popped corn for a lighter crunch

products.title: Ferndale Harlow 31cm Tableware
products.body_html:
The Vintage Inspired Old Leopard Brewery Round Metal Serving Tray brings a bit of old bar-room theatre to drinks, snacks, and gatherings. Made from tinplate metal, it has a deep round shape that feels useful in the hand, with enough height to help keep bottles, glasses, crisps, olives, or small bowls in place as you move from kitchen to table.

  • Round tinplate metal serving tray
  • Vintage Indian beer packaging design
  • Deep well helps steady glasses
  • Approx. 31cm diameter inside
  • Hand wash only after use

Use it for beers in the garden, cocktails before dinner, or a small snack spread when friends arrive early and hover in the kitchen. When it is not being used, it looks happy leaned on a shelf or hung near a home bar.

products.title: Kitchen Table Orbis 31cm Tableware
products.body_html:
The Vintage Inspired Cerveza Espanola Round Metal Serving Tray is made for drinks, snacks, and nibbles. The print has the look of old Spanish beer advertising, with oranges, green leaves, retro lettering, and a woman at the centre of the design. It has that warm holiday-bar feeling without trying too hard.

At 31cm across, it is a useful size for carrying beers, glasses, coffee cups, or a little spread of olives, crisps and tapas. The deep metal well helps keep things contained as you move from kitchen to table, or out into the garden.

  • Vintage Spanish beer advertising style
  • Round tinplate metal serving tray
  • Deep edge helps steady glasses
  • 31cm diameter, 3.8cm deep
  • Hand wash only, not dishwasher safe

It also looks good left out on a bar shelf, drinks trolley, or kitchen wall. A cheerful piece for summer lunches, Friday drinks, or bringing a little Valencia-orange colour to a grey afternoon.

products.title: Daily Basket Tor 31cm Tableware
products.body_html:
The Vintage Inspired Dammer Pils Round Metal Serving Tray is a cheerful bit of barware for drinks, snacks, and nibbles. The artwork has the look of an old European beer advert, with a Dammer Pils logo, a town illustration, and warm reds, yellows and blues across the tray and rim.

  • Vintage German beer-label inspired design
  • Round tinplate tray with raised rim
  • Great for drinks, snacks and bottles
  • Colourful town illustration and retro typography
  • Hand wash only; not dishwasher safe

Internal size is approximately 31cm diameter by 3.8cm high. A lovely gift for someone building a home bar, or anyone who likes their serving pieces with a bit of story and colour.

products.title: Kitchen Table Orbis Tableware
products.body_html:
These Set of 4 Green Dipdye Spiral Candles are for the part of laying the table that feels a bit like play. Tall, twisted taper candles with a dipped colour finish, they bring shape and movement before you’ve even lit them.

They are lovely down the centre of a supper table, on a mantel, or mixed in with plain candles when you want the table to feel gathered rather than arranged. The spiral shape catches the eye, but it does not feel too formal. More “friends coming round” than dinner party panic.

  • Set of four twisted taper candles
  • Dip dye finish with colour variation
  • Each candle measures 20cm tall
  • Made from wax, origin China
  • For dining tables, shelves and celebrations

Use with suitable candle holders and never leave burning candles unattended.

products.title: Pennywise Tor Tableware
products.body_html:
The Set of 4 Dark Grey & Pink Twisted Candles is an easy way to make a table feel more considered, without making it formal. The spiral shape gives height and movement, while the dark grey and pink mix feels modern but still warm. I like them for the kind of supper where the food is simple, the plates don’t quite match, and the candles do a bit of the work.

  • Pack of four twisted taper candles
  • Dark grey and pink colour pairing
  • Each candle measures 20cm tall
  • Made from wax by Rex London
  • Slender 1.8cm taper candle shape

Use them in suitable taper candle holders on a dining table, mantelpiece, or sideboard. The twist catches the eye before they are even lit, which is useful when you want the room to feel ready before anyone arrives.

They are especially good for birthday suppers, winter dinners, or a Friday night table with pasta, salad, bread, and one more glass than planned. Sold as a pack of four.

products.title: Harvest Row Tor Tableware
products.body_html:
The Set of 4 Green & Navy Twisted Candles brings colour, height and a little movement to the table. They are slim wax dinner candles with a spiral shape, made for candlesticks, supper tables, shelves and those evenings when you want the room to feel more gathered.

I like twisted candles because they do a lot without shouting. These have that green and blue mix that works well with simple plates, linen napkins, glass tumblers, and a few bowls of food passed around the table.

  • Pack of four twisted wax candles
  • Green and blue spiral taper design
  • Each candle measures 20cm high
  • Made by Rex London
  • Ideal for dinner tables and mantels

Each candle measures 1.8cm x 1.8cm x 20cm.

products.title: Kitchen Table Nova Tableware
products.body_html:
The Heart Cake Sweet Treat Candle is a playful little home décor candle shaped like a heart-shaped cake. It has a glossy, raspberry-topped look that makes people pause for a second, then smile. Definitely not for eating!

  • Heart-shaped cake design with wax raspberries
  • Playful décor for shelves and tables
  • Part of Rex London’s Sweet Treat range
  • A fun gift for cake lovers

This is one for anyone who likes their homeware with a bit of humour. It sits happily with colourful glassware, birthday cards, little trinket dishes, and all the bits people collect because they make a room feel more alive.

products.title: Pennywise Lumen Tableware
products.body_html:
The Strawberry Hair Claw Clip is a sweet little hair accessory for days when you want your hair up, but still want a bit of fun showing. It has that playful fruit-market feel: red strawberry colour, green leafy detail, and a shape that makes a simple twist or half-up style feel more cheerful.

  • Strawberry design with playful everyday charm
  • Claw clip style for quick up-dos
  • Spring hinge opens and grips hair
  • Useful for medium to long hair
  • A small, easy giftable accessory

Use it for a quick bun before heading out, to keep hair off your neck while cooking, or to add a bright little detail to a plain jumper or summer dress. It is the kind of piece that makes people look twice, in a good way.

products.title: Daily Basket Juno Tableware
products.body_html:
The Orange Hair Claw Clip is a cheerful little hair accessory for days when you want your outfit to feel a bit more sunny. It has that playful fruit-market feel, like something you might pack for a weekend away, wear with a linen shirt, or reach for when your hair needs to be up and out of the way.

  • Orange-themed novelty hair claw clip
  • Useful for buns and half-up styles
  • Bright, playful accessory for everyday wear
  • Lovely for holidays and sunny days

Use it to hold hair back while cooking, travelling, wandering around a market, or sitting outside with something cold to drink. A small thing, yes, but the kind that makes getting ready feel a little more fun.

products.title: Pennywise Wren Tableware
products.body_html:
The Watermelon Hair Claw Clip is a bright little fruit-shaped clip for days when your hair needs holding back, but you still want a bit of fun. It has a watermelon slice design, with red-pink flesh, green rind and dark seed details, plus a shiny finish with hints of marbling and translucence.

Use it to twist up a half-up style, pin back loose pieces, or gather hair off your neck on warm days. It has the familiar claw clip shape, with interlocking teeth and a spring hinge, so it grips sections of hair without needing pins or bands.

  • Fruity watermelon slice hair clip design
  • Red-pink flesh with green rind detail
  • Dark seed accents across the centre
  • Glossy marbled and translucent finish
  • Claw shape grips sections of hair

A cheerful small gift, stocking filler, or treat for someone who likes playful accessories. It is especially lovely for summer outfits, holidays, picnics, or just adding a tiny bit of joy to an ordinary Tuesday.

products.title: Harvest Row Wren Tableware
products.body_html:
The Orange Spritz Claw Clip is a bright, playful hair clip shaped like a summer spritz glass, complete with orange cocktail styling. It has that happy holiday feeling about it. The kind of thing you put in your hair before lunch outside, then forget you are wearing until someone asks where you found it.

  • Spritz-inspired design with orange details
  • Fun choice for summer outfits
  • Easy clip-in hair accessory
  • Great for parties and holidays

Wear it with loose hair, a quick twist, or a messy bun when the weather is warm and nobody wants anything too serious. It is a small accessory, but it changes the mood of an outfit in seconds. Aperitivo energy, without needing to book the flight.

products.title: Greenbank Corin Cookware
products.body_html:
The Fish Stainless Steel Lemon Wedge Squeezer is an iconic tool that makes people smile before they use it. Place a lemon or lime wedge inside the fish-shaped press, squeeze the two sides together, and fresh citrus juice comes out where you want it: over grilled fish, oysters, salads, tea, or a cold drink.

It is made from stainless steel and sized for a generous citrus wedge rather than a whole fruit. I like this sort of squeezer on the table for seafood suppers, because everyone can add their own sharp hit of lemon without chasing pips around the plate.

  • Fish-shaped stainless steel citrus wedge squeezer
  • Made for lemon or lime wedges
  • Helps keep pips off your plate
  • Lovely for seafood, salads and cocktails
  • Manual tool with no batteries needed

A useful little bar and table piece, especially when you want fresh juice from one wedge rather than a bottle from the fridge.

Dimensions: 12.6 × 2.7 × 6.7 cm.

products.title: Harvest Row Wren 10cm Tableware
products.body_html:
The Lime Stoneware Small Bowl is a cheerful little piece of tableware, made for snacks, nibbles, dips and small things that deserve their own place on the table. It has a glossy green glaze with a textured lime-slice pattern, so it brings a fresh hit of colour without taking over the whole setting.

At 10cm wide and 4.3cm high, it is the bowl you reach for when olives need somewhere to go, when the chilli crisp should sit beside the dumplings, or when a few salted nuts appear before dinner. It also looks good left out between meals, which is useful if your table tends to collect nice little bowls anyway.

  • Green lime design with glossy glaze
  • Textured surface inspired by fresh lime
  • Small 10cm bowl for snacks
  • Made from 100% stoneware
  • Designed by Rex London

Use it for lime wedges with tacos, soy sauce beside sushi, pistachios with drinks, or a small handful of sweets after supper. A fun table detail, but a useful one too.

products.title: Harvest Row Nova 15cm Tableware
products.body_html:
The Lime Stoneware Fruit Bowl is a cheerful little piece of tableware for people who like their kitchen to have a bit of wit. It is shaped like a cut lime, with a green glazed finish, citrus segments inside, and a textured rind-like edge. Put it on the table with olives, lime wedges, crisps, sweets, or a handful of cherry tomatoes, and it does that useful thing of making a simple snack feel more considered.

  • Fruit-shaped bowl inspired by a fresh lime
  • Glazed green stoneware with citrus detail
  • Ideal for snacks, dips, or trinkets
  • Playful Rex London tableware design

A lovely gift for anyone who enjoys colourful ceramics, relaxed hosting, or fruit-shaped things that make people smile before dinner has even started.

products.title: Ferndale Solace Tableware
products.body_html:
The Retro glass butter dish is a clear glass butter dish with a simple, old-fashioned feel. It holds a standard 250g block of butter, with a rectangular base and a matching lid embossed with the word “BUTTER”. It is the kind of thing that earns its place on the breakfast table very quickly.

The clear glass means you can see when you are running low, and the raised rim helps the lid sit neatly in place.

  • Clear glass with retro table charm
  • Fits butter blocks up to 250g
  • Embossed “BUTTER” detail on lid
  • Two-piece base and covered lid
  • Dishwasher safe for easy cleaning

Use it on the counter for everyday toast, crumpets and sandwiches, or bring it to the table with warm bread, jam and a pot of tea. It is practical, but it also makes breakfast feel a bit more cared for.

Dimensions: 16.8cm long x 10.2cm wide x 7cm high.

products.title: Daily Basket Solace Tableware
products.body_html:
The Ceramic Toast Trinket Dish is a small glossy ceramic dish shaped like a slice of toast. It is made for the little things that vanish just when you need them. Rings beside the bed. Coins by the door. Keys on the hallway table. A tiny dish with a sense of humour.

We like pieces like this because they make everyday clutter feel less annoying. It is practical, but it also makes you smile when you put your earrings down at night.

  • Glossy ceramic with smooth glazed finish
  • Shaped like a slice of toast
  • Useful for keys, coins and jewellery
  • Fun gift for homeware lovers
  • Lovely on bedside or hallway tables

Use it for rings, hair clips, spare change, lip balm, or the key you always swear you left “somewhere obvious”. It is not sold as tableware, but as a trinket dish for small treasures and everyday bits.

products.title: Greenbank Wren Tableware
products.body_html:
The Ceramic trinket dish - Fried egg is a small white ceramic dish, shaped like a sunny fried egg. It is made for the little things that always seem to wander off. Rings by the sink. Keys near the door. A pair of earrings taken off while making tea.

It has that cheerful, slightly daft charm that makes people smile before they even ask what it is. I like pieces like this because they do a simple job, but bring a bit of breakfast-table joy to a bedside table, hallway shelf, or bathroom windowsill.

  • White ceramic fried egg trinket dish
  • Useful for rings, keys, earrings
  • Playful gift for food lovers
  • Made by Rex London

A lovely little present for someone who loves eggs, brunch, or useful things with a sense of humour. Also very good for anyone who says they never lose their keys, while always losing their keys.

products.title: Ferndale Mira Tableware
products.body_html:
The Sausage Dog Claw Clip is a playful hair accessory for anyone who has a soft spot for dachshunds. The long sausage dog shape works so well as a claw clip, with the dog’s body forming the grip and hinged teeth holding your hair in place. It is the kind of small thing that makes getting ready feel a bit more fun.

Made with a marble resin finish, it has a swirled look rather than a flat block colour. Wear it for a quick twist, a half-up style, or just to keep your hair off your face while cooking, reading, or heading out for coffee.

  • Shaped like a sweet sausage dog
  • Marble resin finish with swirled detail
  • Hinged claw teeth grip hair securely
  • Playful gift for dachshund lovers
  • Best wiped clean by hand

A lovely little gift, or treat for yourself if dogs tend to make their way into your mugs, tea towels, notebooks, and now your hair.

Meet the maker: Sass & Belle

Sass & Belle is an independent London brand, creating cheerful gifts and homeware since 2009. Their pieces are cute, charming and playful, with a simple aim: to make you smile.

If you enjoy kitchenware with warmth, humour and a touch of whimsy, Sass & Belle is a lovely place to start.

products.body_html:

Pop it in for a quick half-up style, twist it into a loose bun, or keep it in your bag for hair that needs sorting halfway through the day.

  • Bright red cherry-shaped hair claw clip
  • Made from resin with glossy finish
  • Useful for quick on-the-go styling
  • Keeps hair held neatly in place
  • A fun small gift or treat

  • Red berry design with green leaves
  • Spring hinge with interlocking teeth
  • Lovely small gift or stocking filler
  • Fun for casual everyday styling

Lakrids by Bülow was founded in Denmark by Johan Bülow in 2007, with the idea that liquorice could behave like a spice. Here it meets white chocolate, vanilla and Japanese citrus, and the result is playful without being childish.

Meet the maker: Lakrids

Lakrids liquorice comes all the way from one of the finest liquorice producers in Denmark, the home of liquorice. In 2007, Lakrids started as the dream of Johan Bülow, who didn’t understand why liquorice was so rarely blended with other flavours. Nor why liquorice had traditionally been made using wheat flour, instead of a gluten free flour. It turns out that both are very difficult! But with much trial and error, Johan Bülow started to produce some of the finest liquorice in the world. Lakrids liquorice is only made with gluten free rice flour, and he treats liquorice as a spice – one which enhances and perfectly complements other flavours.

Meet the maker: Neuhaus

Neuhaus Chocolates are one of the finest chocolate houses in Belgium – and perhaps the world. The silky smooth chocolate is beautifully delicate and has a wonderful snap, all blended with exquisite ingredients, carefully sourced for the very best flavour. The iconic chocolatiers are also heralded as the inventors of Belgian filled pralines. Neuhaus uses 100% sustainably sourced cacao for their chocolates as well as investing in their own cacao plantation in Ecuador. He opened a pharmacy in Brussels, and as a way to thrill his customers, he covered their medicines in a thin layer of chocolate. Fast forward to 1912, Jean’s grandson swapped medicine for an indulgent chocolate centre, inventing what we now know and love as the praline.

Spice Kitchen began around a family kitchen table, with Shashi blending spices by hand and her son Sanjay turning that care into a small business. Their now-famous masala dabba spice tins are inspired by the traditional tins used in Indian homes, where cooking starts with colour, scent and a little daily ritual.

What I love about Spice Kitchen is how joyful and useful their products feel. These are fresh, small-batch blends made to help you cook with more confidence, whether you are making a curry, brewing chai, or trying a new flavour from another part of the world. It is spice with a story, made by people who understand how food brings people closer.

Meet the maker: Olio Anfosso

Olio Anfosso comes from Chiusavecchia, a small olive-growing village tucked inland from the Ligurian coast. The Anfosso family has been making extra virgin olive oil here since 1945, when Davide Anfosso began tending a small grove after the war. Three generations later, their oils still carry the gentle, coastal character of western Liguria: soft, fruity, and made for food rather than fuss.

This is the kind of producer that makes you want to slow down and cook simply. Think warm potatoes, grilled fish, bitter leaves, focaccia, or a bowl of beans finished with a bright green pour. Olio Anfosso is rooted in family, stone terraces, and the old olive culture of the Ponente - and that care shows in every bottle.

Lakrids by Bülow SYRUP / Liquid Liquorice is a dark, pourable liquorice syrup for any cook who likes strong flavours, that add real interest to a recipe or dessert.

It has deep molasses sweetness first, then the liquorice comes through, rounded with vanilla and a small pinch of salt. Try it over vanilla ice cream to instantly understand its full flavour profile.

  • Made with 9% raw liquorice
  • Dark molasses sweetness and vanilla notes
  • Pour over ice cream or pancakes
  • Use in baking, cooking, or cocktails
  • Organic, gluten-free, and gelatine-free

We like this where you would use a dark caramel, but want something less expected. Ripple it through brownie batter, spoon a little into a whisky cocktail, or drizzle it over roasted pears with cream. A small amount goes a long way, so start with less than you think.

Meet the maker: Lakrids

Lakrids liquorice comes all the way from one of the finest liquorice producers in Denmark, the home of liquorice. In 2007, Lakrids started as the dream of Johan Bülow, who didn’t understand why liquorice was so rarely blended with other flavours. Nor why liquorice had traditionally been made using wheat flour, instead of a gluten free flour. It turns out that both are very difficult! But with much trial and error, Johan Bülow started to produce some of the finest liquorice in the world. Lakrids liquorice is only made with gluten free rice flour, and he treats liquorice as a spice – one which enhances and perfectly complements other flavours.

Product formulations and details may change. For the latest ingredients and allergen information always check product packaging prior to consumption. Ingredients: Sugar*, glucose syrup*, molasses*, 9% raw liquorice* (non-eu), water, salt, acid: citric acid, vanilla*. *=organic.

The Seikou Porcelain Birds on Branch Japanese Teapot is a Kutani ware teapot from Seikou kiln in Ishikawa Prefecture, Japan. It brings that lovely teapot moment of theatre to the table: leaves steeping, cups waiting, and a painted bird-and-branch design that gives you something to look at while everyone slows down for five minutes.

Seikou has been making Kutani porcelain since 1935, with a focus on traditional Japanese enamel colours in more modern shapes and patterns. This piece has the nature detail the kiln is known for, with fine painting and a luminous glazed finish. It is made for serving tea, but it also earns its place when left out on a shelf between uses.

  • Japanese Kutani porcelain from Seikou kiln
  • Made in Ishikawa Prefecture, Japan
  • Birds on branch nature motif
  • Colourful overglaze enamel Kutani decoration
  • Beautiful enough to leave on display

Use it for green tea after lunch, hojicha in the afternoon, or a pot of something gentle when friends stay too long at the table. It also makes a thoughtful gift for someone who loves Japanese tableware, tea rituals, or small objects with a story behind them.

Meet the maker: Seikou

Japanese artisans, Seikou, started producing signature hand-painted porcelain nearly a hundred years ago. The family-owned business is loved in Japan for its ko-kutani style. Kutani-yaki, or kutani-ware, is a technique that uses thick overglaze, bold colours and hand-painted detail. Kutani-ware pieces are often decorated with flowers, animals and geometric motifs.

Seikou porcelain uses traditional techniques to create colourful, contemporary crockery that is both beautiful and practical. As well as intricate floral patterns, you'll find playful motifs such as dancing pandas, and charming bluebirds. Use your Seikou tableware to create a richly patterned tablescape, with bold bright colours. Mix and match your favourite motifs, or choose a set with the same pattern.

  • Hand-picked and jarred on the farm
  • Crunchy texture with clean vinegar bite
  • Made without added chemical preservatives
  • Grown without herbicides or insecticides

Serve with charcuterie, rillettes, terrines, raclette, fondue, or a very good ham sandwich. Also worth putting out with drinks before dinner. People always seem to take one, then come back for three more.

Meet the maker: Maison Marc

What makes them special is the short journey from field to jar. Maison Marc grows its own cornichons in Burgundy, then harvests and packs them in France. Their cornichons are grown without herbicides or insecticides, picked by hand, and jarred without preservatives.

For anyone who loves French food, Maison Marc is a lovely discovery: real Burgundy-grown cornichons, made with patience, care and a deep respect for a classic French staple.

Embark on a delightful culinary adventure with Manon Lagrève’s third cookbook, La Saison. This enchanting collection proves that French cuisine can be savoured throughout the seasons. Let Manon guide you from her charming London home kitchen to her family's heartwarming kitchen in France, as she celebrates the finest produce each season has to offer.

From the crisp, refreshing salads of summer to the soul-warming stews of winter, La Saison is your ticket to a year-round feast of flavours. Each chapter begins with a seasonal tipsheet, showcasing the freshest fruits, vegetables, poultry and fish to inspire your shopping list. Manon’s French heritage and effortless approach to seasonal eating are at the heart of this book, making it easy for you to embrace this philosophy too.

Designed for the modern home cook, the recipes blend traditional French flavours with clever shortcuts, ensuring minimal time in the kitchen without compromising on taste. Whether you’re preparing a quick weeknight dinner or a lavish celebratory feast, her recipes are perfect for any occasion. Celebrate your favourite holidays with Manon's delightful creations, from an elegant Easter lunch with cake, to a festive Christmas dinner and seasonal tipple.

With over 80 accessible recipes, La Saison will inspire you to replicate the seasonal French way of eating, no matter where you are in the world.

They make certified organic chocolate bars and drinking chocolate with ethically sourced cacao, natural ingredients, and bold, art-led packaging. Ocelot was founded in 2014 by husband-and-wife team Matt and Ishbel Broadbent. It began as a kitchen-table project in Edinburgh and grew into a small-batch craft chocolate brand with a dedicated workshop. Ocelot’s packaging is part of the joy. Each bar is wrapped in bold, graphic artwork, with a different design for each flavour. It makes the chocolate feel special before you even open it.

This is chocolate with a strong sense of place and purpose. Ocelot uses 100% regenerative chocolate, made with cacao grown in ways that help restore soil health and support biodiversity. Their cacao is ethically sourced by Original Beans, who work to make sure farmers are fairly paid.

The flavour combinations are thoughtful and food-led. Think fruit, citrus, coffee, sea salt, and other natural ingredients paired with high-quality single-origin chocolate. The range includes dark, milk, and white chocolate styles, with some vegan-friendly dark bars depending on the recipe.

It has that clean mustard heat you want from Dijon: sharp enough to wake up a ham sandwich, useful enough to stir into vinaigrette, and punchy enough to sit beside roast chicken without disappearing.

  • Classic smooth Dijon mustard texture
  • Bright heat from mustard seeds
  • Packed on the farm in Burgundy
  • Made by independent family producer Maison Marc
  • Glass jar, useful everyday size

Maison Marc has been making French cornichons since 1923, and their condiments carry the same practical, table-ready feel. This is not a mustard to save at the back of the cupboard. Keep it close for sausages, rare roast beef, cheese toasties, lentil salads, potato salad, or a quick pan sauce with cream and white wine.

Meet the maker: Maison Marc

Maison Marc makes French cornichons and condiments in Chemilly-sur-Yonne, in Burgundy. Their best-known jars are the small, crisp cornichons that make a cheese board, pâté, terrine or raclette feel complete.

What makes them special is the short journey from field to jar. Maison Marc grows its own cornichons in Burgundy, then harvests and packs them in France. Their cornichons are grown without herbicides or insecticides, picked by hand, and jarred without preservatives.

These are the cornichons you want beside rich food: bright, sharp, firm and clean-tasting. They cut through charcuterie and potato salads, or lift a sandwich. The jars are simple and elegant too, with clear glass and well-designed labels. They look right at home on the table, not hidden away in the fridge door.

For anyone who loves French food, Maison Marc is a lovely discovery: real Burgundy-grown cornichons, made with patience, care and a deep respect for a classic French staple.

Spice Kitchen Street Food Supper Feasting Kit is made for the night when you want dinner to feel a bit more like an event. Inside the tin are four small-batch spice blends — Jerk, Tandoori Masala, Cajun and Piri Piri - plus recipe cards, a shopping list and Spice Kitchen’s measuring spoon. It takes away the “what shall we cook?” bit and leaves you with the good part: marinating, sizzling, tasting, and putting a table full of colourful dishes in front of people.

  • Four Great Taste award-winning spice blends
  • Includes recipe cards and shopping list
  • Comes with Spice Kitchen measuring spoon
  • Reusable tin keeps spices neatly stored
  • Vegetarian alternatives included with each recipe

The recipes lean into street-food suppers: Piri Piri chicken, tandoori lamb chops, spiced slaw, Cajun rice and hot garlic mayo. The kind of food where plates get passed around and someone always wants a second spoonful of the mayo.

Blended in small batches by family-run Spice Kitchen in Liverpool, this is a lovely gift for curious cooks, beginner spice explorers, or anyone who likes a Friday night fakeaway with a bit more hands-on fun.

Meet the maker: Spice Kitchen

Spice Kitchen began around a family kitchen table, with Shashi blending spices by hand and her son Sanjay turning that care into a small business. Their now-famous masala dabba spice tins are inspired by the traditional tins used in Indian homes, where cooking starts with colour, scent and a little daily ritual.

What I love about Spice Kitchen is how joyful and useful their products feel. These are fresh, small-batch blends made to help you cook with more confidence, whether you are making a curry, brewing chai, or trying a new flavour from another part of the world. It is spice with a story, made by people who understand how food brings people closer.

Olio Anfosso Tumai Monocultivar Taggiasca extra virgin olive oil is made in Chiusavecchia, Liguria, from 100% Taggiasca olives. It has that lovely soft Ligurian character: golden in the glass, with green flashes, a gentle almond note, and the green smell of herbs, artichoke and tomato leaf.

This is a bottle we reach for when the oil matters. Not just for cooking, but for finishing. Spoon it over warm beans, grilled vegetables, soup, bruschetta, or a simple plate of tomatoes with salt. It brings flavour without shouting over the food.

  • 100% Taggiasca olives from Liguria
  • Cold extracted in the family mill
  • Golden yellow with greenish hues
  • Soft almond, herb and artichoke notes
  • Lovely on bruschetta, soups and vegetables

It is made by Olio Anfosso, a family producer with more than 70 years of olive oil tradition. The oil may show a little natural sediment, as it is reported to be unfiltered. Give the bottle a moment, pour generously, and let it do the small but important work at the table.

Meet the maker: Olio Anfosso

Olio Anfosso comes from Chiusavecchia, a small olive-growing village tucked inland from the Ligurian coast. The Anfosso family has been making extra virgin olive oil here since 1945, when Davide Anfosso began tending a small grove after the war. Three generations later, their oils still carry the gentle, coastal character of western Liguria: soft, fruity, and made for food rather than fuss.

This is the kind of producer that makes you want to slow down and cook simply. Think warm potatoes, grilled fish, bitter leaves, focaccia, or a bowl of beans finished with a bright green pour. Olio Anfosso is rooted in family, stone terraces, and the old olive culture of the Ponente - and that care shows in every bottle.

Product formulations and details may change. For the latest ingredients and allergen information always check product packaging prior to consumption. Ingredients: Extra virgin olive oil .

Greek Style Sliced Chorizo from The Greek Farmer is a ready-to-eat cured pork charcuterie made with British free-range pork, red wine, garlic, paprika and a little cayenne. It has the familiar paprika warmth of chorizo, but the flavour is very mild, so it works well when you want savoury depth without a big chilli hit.

  • Mild paprika warmth, not fierce heat
  • Made with British free-range pork
  • Ready-sliced and ready to serve
  • Greek-influenced British farm charcuterie

The 70g pack is useful when you want a grazing board without getting the knife out. Open it, lay the slices with olives, cheeses, bread and something sharp like pickles or cornichons, and you have a small plate that feels considered without much work.

It is also good tucked into a picnic bag, added to a charcuterie platter, or served before dinner with a glass of red wine while everyone hovers near the kitchen.

Meet the maker: The Greek Farmer

The Greek Farmer makes British charcuterie with a Greek twist, using British free-range pork and curing it on their farm in Hertfordshire. Think salami and air-dried meats with that sunny, savoury lift you get from Mediterranean herbs and spices. It is the kind of food that turns a simple board of cheese, bread and olives into something people gather around.

Small, family-run and proudly farm-based, they bring together proper British pork with flavours inspired by Greek recipes. Their award-winning range feels made for sharing: picnics, picky dinners, drinks with friends, or the moment when you “just slice a little” and somehow go back for more.

The Silverwood Bakeware Silver Anodised Spherical Pudding Mould is made for those wonderful round puddings that arrive at the table with a bit of theatre. Christmas pudding, steamed sponge, summer pudding, an ice cream bombe for a birthday lunch; this is the tin you reach for when a normal basin feels a bit too ordinary.

It is made from Silverwood’s silver anodised aluminium, which conducts heat quickly and evenly. That matters with steamed and baked puddings, where you want the centre cooked through without the outside turning heavy.

  • 6 inch spherical pudding mould
  • Made from anodised aluminium
  • Handmade in Birmingham, England
  • Naturally non-stick, uncoated surface
  • Oven safe for baking puddings

The pale silver finish is practical rather than showy. It feels like traditional British bakeware: light in the hand, strong enough for years of use, and made for cooks who like doing things properly without making a fuss about it.

Hand wash in warm soapy water, dry well, and avoid metal scourers.

Meet the maker: Silverwood Bakeware

Silverwood bakeware is handmade in Birmingham, England, where they have been making tins since the 1960s. It's high quality, hardworking bakeware made for people who love a clean edge, an even bake, and that small moment of joy when something lifts out beautifully.

Silverwood’s anodised aluminium also has a naturally easy-release surface that improves with use. A light grease is still wise, especially for sticky bakes, but this is not a coated tin that flakes or peels. It is strong, light to handle, and made to be used often.

We love that Silverwood still makes in the UK, by hand, in a city with a long metalworking history. This is not bakeware pretending to be special. It is special because it has been thought through by people who understand baking, and will last and last.

If you care about neat brownies, even traybakes, and kitchen tools that feel dependable from the first use, Silverwood is a maker worth knowing.

The Silverwood Bakeware Silver Anodised Loaf Tin with Loose Base is the kind of tin you reach for when you want bread with a good crust, a loaf cake that comes out in one piece, or a meatloaf that slices neatly for supper. It is handmade by Silverwood in Birmingham, using strong but lightweight anodised aluminium that spreads heat evenly through the tin.

The loose base is especially useful for softer bakes. Think lemon drizzle, banana bread, ginger loaf, terrines, or anything sticky around the edges. Instead of tipping the whole thing upside down and hoping for the best, you can ease the bake out with more control.

  • Handmade in Birmingham, England
  • Silver anodised aluminium for even baking
  • Loose base helps with easy release
  • Strong, lightweight, professional-grade construction
  • Naturally non-stick surface develops with use

Silverwood tins do not use a non-stick coating. The anodised aluminium surface itself becomes more naturally non-stick as it is used and cared for. It also heats quickly and cools faster than heavier tins, which helps stop a loaf carrying on too much once it leaves the oven.

Wash by hand in warm soapy water, rinse, and dry well. Avoid sharp knives in the tin, and do not put it in the dishwasher. Treat it well, and it should become one of those tins that lives within easy reach, ready for the next loaf.

Meet the maker: Silverwood Bakeware

Silverwood bakeware is handmade in Birmingham, England, where they have been making tins since the 1960s. It's high quality, hardworking bakeware made for people who love a clean edge, an even bake, and that small moment of joy when something lifts out beautifully.

Silverwood’s anodised aluminium also has a naturally easy-release surface that improves with use. A light grease is still wise, especially for sticky bakes, but this is not a coated tin that flakes or peels. It is strong, light to handle, and made to be used often.

We love that Silverwood still makes in the UK, by hand, in a city with a long metalworking history. This is not bakeware pretending to be special. It is special because it has been thought through by people who understand baking, and will last and last.

If you care about neat brownies, even traybakes, and kitchen tools that feel dependable from the first use, Silverwood is a maker worth knowing.

products.title: Kitchen Table Aria Cookware
products.body_html:
This French tea towel is a celebration of citrus. It’s made from 100% cotton in a vibrant shade of orange. The woven design features juicy oranges, both sliced and whole.

The material is soft and absorbent - ideal for drying dishes and polishing glasses. You can also use it to carry hot pans and plates to the table. With its bright orange hue, it looks great on a hook when not in use.

The towel is made using the Jacquard technique. The design is woven directly into the fabric, rather than screen printed. This makes the towel more durable and resistant to fading.

About Tissage Moutet

Since 1913, five generations of the Moutet family have been weaving exceptional linen in the foothills of the Pyrenees. Their traditional looms create textiles with an unmistakable hand-feel - soft yet substantial, beautiful yet built to last decades.

When you choose Tissage Moutet, you're not just buying linen. You're investing in French heritage. The linens have the geographical certification Basque Linen. You're supporting artisan craftsmanship, and finding home something genuinely special that improves with every wash.

products.title: Greenbank Corin 16cm Cookware
products.body_html:
The Netherton Foundry Spun Iron Burger Dome is a small piece of kit that makes a real difference at the hob, on the barbecue, or over an open fire.

Pop it over a burger and the heat gathers inside, melting cheese down the sides instead of leaving it sitting stubbornly on top. It is also useful for covered cooking, baking, warming bread, or helping food cook through without drying out.

  • Spun from 99.1% pure iron
  • Pre-seasoned with edible Sussex flax oil
  • Retains heat for even melting
  • Use indoors, outdoors, oven or barbecue
  • No chemical coating, no PTFE

The dome has a cast iron knob and stainless steel fittings, so it is happy over flames as well as in the oven. It fits Netherton frying pans and prospector pans from 18cm upwards, and its 16cm diameter is just right for burgers, breakfast muffins, or a small stack of vegetables.

Like Netherton’s pans, it comes ready to use with a baked-on flax oil seasoning. Wash by hand, dry well, and refresh the coating at home when needed. Simple, tough, repairable cookware from Shropshire, made for the meals people cook together.

Meet the maker: Netherton Foundry

In the hills of South Shropshire, Netherton Foundry makes iron cookware with a very simple idea at its heart: good pans should last, be repaired, be re-seasoned, and be used often. This small, family-owned British maker works in a part of the UK known as the birthplace of the Industrial Revolution.

Their spun iron pieces are formed on lathes, then seasoned in-house with edible Sussex flax oil. That baked-on oil gives the cookware its dark, matte finish and helps create a naturally non-stick surface. There is no PTFE and no chemical coating. Just iron, oil, heat, and time.

That is one of the things we love about Netherton Foundry. Their cookware asks you to be part of the story. You use it, wash it, dry it, and every so often you give it a little oil and heat. If the seasoning wears, you restore it. If it gets a rust spot, you clean it back and build it up again. It is a lovely, low-waste way to cook.

If you like tools with a sense of place, and you enjoy the small rituals of good cooking, Netherton Foundry is a maker worth getting to know.

products.title: Daily Basket Kite Tableware
products.body_html:
The Opinel Le Petit Gourmet Green 3 Piece Children’s Cutlery Set is a lovely first table set for a child who wants to join in at mealtimes. It includes a knife, fork and spoon, shaped for small hands and designed to help children learn how to eat with cutlery.

What we love about this set is that it feels grown-up without being too grown-up. Children notice that. They want the fork that looks like yours, the spoon that belongs to them, the little knife for spreading butter on toast or cutting soft food with help nearby.

  • Knife, fork and spoon included
  • Made for small children’s hands
  • Helps build independent eating skills
  • Cutlery joins together for storage
  • Stainless steel with wooden-style handles

Opinel has been making knives and tools in Savoie, France since 1890, and this children’s cutlery set carries that same practical, family-table feeling. It is part of the Le Petit Gourmet range, made for young children learning to eat with confidence.

Best washed by hand and dried after use, especially because of the wooden handles. Suitable for supervised mealtimes.

Meet the maker: Opinel

Opinel began in 1890 in the Savoie region of France, when Joseph Opinel created a simple folding knife for everyday working people.

More than 130 years later, Opinel is still closely tied to that same place. Its knives and tools are made in Chambéry, in the French Alps, and the brand has become one of those rare kitchen names that feels both practical and full of heritage.

products.title: Ferndale Atlas 250ml Ingredient
products.body_html:
Ester Ispirata alla Salsa Worcestershire Sauce is an Italian-made seasoning sauce inspired by the classic English cupboard staple. It has that dark, tangy, savoury-sweet character you want from a Worcestershire-style sauce, but without anchovies A few shakes bring vinegar, molasses, tamarind, garlic, ginger and clove into the pan. Useful stuff.

  • Sweet-sour, savoury, lightly spiced flavour
  • Anchovy-free Worcestershire-style Italian sauce
  • Made with grape must and tamarind
  • Glass bottle for easy cupboard storage

Use it where you want depth without making the dish taste “saucy”. Stir a little into stews, tomato sauces, veggie chilli, burger mix, marinades or mushroom gravy. It is also very good in a Bloody Mary, especially if you like the drink with more bite than sweetness.

Store in a cool, dry place.

Product formulations and details may change. For the latest ingredients and allergen information always check product packaging prior to consumption. Ingredients: Grape must, wine vinegar, water, sugar, spirit vinegar, molasses, onions, salt, tamarind extract, natural flavourings, cloves, ginger, garlic, modified starch. Contains: sulphites.

products.title: Kitchen Table Harlow Ingredient
products.body_html:
Leone Milk Chocolate Block with Hazelnuts is a generous Italian milk chocolate block studded with whole Piedmont hazelnuts. The chocolate is creamy and sweet, made with unrefined raw cane sugar, cocoa butter, whole milk powder, cocoa paste and cocoa beans. Then come the hazelnuts: crisp, round, and visible when you break the block into pieces.

This is the kind of chocolate to put in the middle of the table after lunch. People snap off a piece, then come back for another. The Piedmont hazelnuts give it a real crunch, with that warm, toasted nut flavour that works so well against milk chocolate.

  • Italian milk chocolate with Piedmont hazelnuts
  • Whole nuts give a crisp, clean crunch
  • Made with unrefined raw cane sugar
  • Large block for sharing and gifting

Serve with coffee, tea, or a glass of dessert wine. You can also chop it into brownies, cookies, or rocky road when you want both chocolate and hazelnut in every bite.

Meet the maker: Leone

Leone has been making some of the finest sweets in Italy since 1857. Luigi Leone opened his first shop in Collegno, Piedmont to sell digestive pastilles. His mint, cinnamon and clove-flavoured delights proved so popular that before long he found himself opening a shop in Turin. His customers even included the Royal House of Savoy. Today Leone continues to make sweets using the finest Italian ingredients. They stay rooted in Luigi’s original goal: 'to bring small moments of happiness to those who savour their products'.

Product formulations and details may change. For the latest ingredients and allergen information always check product packaging prior to consumption. Ingredients: Milk chocolate (unrefined raw cane sugar, cocoa butter, whole milk powder (20%), cocoa paste and cocoa beans), "piedmont hazelnut" (10%).

Allergy advice: For allergens see ingredients in bold. May contain: may contain tree nuts (pistachios, almonds).

products.title: Harvest Row Mira Cookware
products.body_html:
This set of four Laguiole en Aubrac steak knives features elegant maple wood handles with an eye-catching wavy pattern. They are a perfect gift for any food lover that enjoys cooking steaks at home. Handcrafted in France, the razor sharp blades glide easily through veal chops, pork belly and Chateaubriand.

The knives are made with Sandvik stainless steel which is incredibly robust and corrosion-resistant. It retains its sharp edge over time and has a curved tip for a smooth, even finish on every slice. Forged from a single piece of steel, these beautiful balanced knives deliver a powerfully clean cut, even on well done meat.

This set of four Laguiole en Aubrac steak knives is presented in a wooden box with a certificate of authenticity.

About Laguiole en Aubrac

Laguiole en Aubrac brought the art of knife-making back to Espalion in the 20th century, creating the highest quality, artisanal stainless steel knives. The original Laguiole knife dates back to 1829, when a simple folding knife became the talk of not only the town, but the whole country, loved for its practicality and elegant, intricate design.

Fast forward to the 21st century and Laguiole en Aubrac are lovingly creating knives once again. All knives are individually hardened by hand; shaping and fitting are done by hand to the craftsman’s eye. Each knife is assembled from start to finish in one sequence and by a single craftsman. 

All Laguiole en Aubrac knives come with a lifetime guarantee – they’re a name and knife you can trust.

Handmade in France, this set of four steak knives makes a wonderful gift or a stylish addition to your own dining table. The ultra-sharp blades have curved tips which give a smooth, even finish to every slice.

The knives are crafted from Sandvik stainless steel to produce incredibly robust blades that are high-wear and corrosion-resistant. Beautifully balanced and razor sharp, these elegant steak knives glide effortlessly through your favourite cuts of meat. products.title: Daily Basket Pike 560ml Ingredient
products.body_html:
Fabbri Zero Amarena Cherry Syrup gives you the dark cherry flavour of Fabbri’s Amarena range without added sugar. And in fact, many if our tasters couldn't tell the difference. It is made with concentrated wild cherry juice and has the deep colour you want from a cherry syrup, so drinks still look generous rather than apologetic.

  • Zero sugar Amarena cherry syrup
  • Made with 45% concentrated wild cherry juice
  • Fewer than 4 calories per 100ml when prepared as a drink
  • Use for sodas, mocktails, milkshakes and desserts

Pour a little over ice and top with sparkling water, or use it for yoghurt, panna cotta, chocolate ice cream and cherry-led cocktails. It is useful when you want cherry flavour without making the drink thick or sticky.

About The Maker: Fabbri

Fabbri was founded in Bologna in 1905 by Gennaro Fabbri, whose preserved Amarena cherries became one of Italy’s most recognisable pantry products. The blue-and-white ceramic jars are now almost as famous as the cherries themselves. More than a century later, the brand still feels deeply tied to Italian café and dessert culture. There’s nostalgia to Fabbri, but it remains genuinely loved rather than simply historic.

Product formulations and details may change. For the latest ingredients and allergen information always check product packaging prior to consumption. Ingredients: Water, wild cherry juice (45%) conc, acid citric acid, vegetable concentrate (carrot, blackcurrant), flavourings, preservatives e 202 (potassium sorbate), e 211 (sodium benzoate), sweeteners sucralose, acesulfame-k.

products.title: Ferndale Kite Ingredient
products.body_html:
Whole Pink Pralines 15% Almonds are the bright, crunchy French sweets you see scattered through Lyon-style brioche and baking. Each whole almond is wrapped in a hard pink sugar shell, giving you that mix of roasted nut, caramelised sweetness, and a little theatre on the worktop.

  • Whole almonds with crisp pink sugar shells
  • Classic for brioche aux pralines roses
  • Crunchy texture with roasted almond flavour
  • Made in traditional copper cauldrons
  • 500g bag for baking or snacking

Use them whole in brioche de Saint-Genix, chop them into cake batter, or crush a few over vanilla ice cream. The shell is hard, so use a sturdy knife or rolling pin. In baking, they soften and bleed a little pink into doughs and creams, which is half the fun.

Meet the maker: Miel Besacier

Miel Besacier is a French honey house, and pralines producer.

Founded in 1905, this family-run company has spent more than a century working with honey, bees, and beekeepers. Today it is led by David Besacier, who is also President of the French Honey Association. So this is not a brand that simply buys honey and puts a label on it. Honey is their world.

What we love about Miel Besacier is how close they stay to the source. They select honey directly from beekeepers, build long-term partnerships, and put a strong focus on traceability.

Miel Besacier has also spent more than 30 years focused on organic production and better beekeeping practices. Not every jar is automatically certified organic, so check the product title and label if that is important to you.

Product formulations and details may change. For the latest ingredients and allergen information always check product packaging prior to consumption. Ingredients: Sugar, almonds (nuts) (15%), glucose syrup, arabic gum, flavouring, colors (E129* - E120) (*may cause behavioural and attention disorders in children)

Fold them into brioche dough, scatter over meringues before baking, or spoon over vanilla ice cream at the table. Instant joy and texture!

  • French-style pink caramelised almond praline
  • Crushed texture for easy baking
  • Bright colour for desserts and toppings
